title: One Relocated Verifier Step
statement: Let $S$ and $V$ be finite deterministic Turing machines over the binary alphabet, let $x,y$ be binary inputs, and let $c$ be a nonhalted configuration of $V$ on $y$. Suppose a Boolean tag correctly marks the boundary whenever the virtual input head is at either endpoint. Choose any input-head position for $x$, any contents for the work tapes of $S$, any work-head positions for $S$, and any choice bit. There is a Boolean tag correctly marking the boundary for the virtual input-head position after one step of $V$ such that one host step from the corresponding verifier-phase configuration equals the verifier-phase configuration formed from the successor of $c$, with the chosen scheduler data unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: A configuration $c$ of $V$ on $y$ with nonhalted state
An initial Boolean tag satisfying the virtual boundary condition
Arbitrary contents of the scheduler work tapes
replaced: Let $S, V$ be deterministic machines, $d$ a non-halted verifier configuration on an assembled word $y$ carrying a valid virtual boundary tag, and fix frozen scheduler data and a physical position. For every choice bit, one host step maps the verifier-phase configuration for $d$ to the verifier-phase configuration for the stepped verifier, with some valid updated tag; reads come from the assembly buffer and every emission of $V$ is captured, including one on a halting transition.
